about: The introit of the Second Sunday of Advent, from Isaias, with a verse of Psalm 79. The antiphon addresses the people of Sion and says what the Lord comes for — to save the nations, and to let His voice be heard.

seg.tr: O people of Sion, behold, the Lord will come to save the nations; the Lord will make the glory of His voice heard for the joy of your hearts.
You who shepherd Israel, give ear; You who lead Joseph like a sheep.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

fn.w029: The doxology has no expressed verb. It supplies the wish “glory be” from liturgical usage.

seg.nr: After the doxology the Introit antiphon is repeated from Pópulus Sion to the psalm verse — by the choir at a sung Mass, by the priest himself at a low Mass.

seg.tr: O people of Sion, behold, the Lord will come to save the nations; the Lord will make the glory of His voice heard for the joy of your hearts.
